title: Retry rule: 1000
means: The documented retry expression is evaluated after each failed delivery, with retried starting at zero; the endpoint here returns 503.

title: Retry rule: 1000 * (1 + retried)
means: The documented retry expression is evaluated after each failed delivery, with retried starting at zero; the endpoint here returns 503.

title: Retry rule: pow(2, retried) * 1000
means: The documented retry expression is evaluated after each failed delivery, with retried starting at zero; the endpoint here returns 503.

title: Retry rule: max(1000, pow(2, retried) * 100)
means: The documented retry expression is evaluated after each failed delivery, with retried starting at zero; the endpoint here returns 503.

title: Flow control rule: ten calls in the first minute, the next waits for the next period
means: Rate 10 per minute with parallelism 20 sends ten calls in the first minute, and the next in the next minute.

title: Retry expression function: sqrt
means: The documented sqrt function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: abs
means: The documented abs function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: exp
means: The documented exp function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: floor
means: The documented floor function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: ceil
means: The documented ceil function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: round
means: The documented round function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Retry expression function: min
means: The documented min function computes the millisecond delay of the next attempt; the World supplies its numeric arguments and a failing endpoint.

title: Flow control rule: rate period defaults to one second
means: By default the rate period is one second; rate 1 holds the second call until that second passes.

title: Failure callback rule: its own retries, retry delay and method
means: Upstash-Failure-Callback-Retries, -Retry-Delay and -Method configure the failure callback's own message: the message is not retried (Upstash-Retries: 0) while its failure callback, answered 503, is retried once, a second later, with PUT.

title: Callback rule: its own delay, timeout, retries and method
means: Upstash-Callback-Delay, -Timeout, -Retries and -Method configure the callback's own message (the callbacks page: "the Upstash-Callback / Upstash-Failure-Callback prefix can be used to configure callbacks"): delivered ten seconds after the message, with PUT, given up after five seconds on an answer that takes ten, and not retried.

title: Failure callback rule: its own flow control
means: Upstash-Failure-Callback-Flow-Control-Key and -Value limit the failure callbacks: two messages failing at once call their failure callbacks one per minute (rate 1, period 1m).

title: Retry rule: 489 with Upstash-NonRetryable-Error: true is not retried
means: A 489 with the header Upstash-NonRetryable-Error: true fails the message at once, without its retries, into the DLQ.

title: Retry rule: 489 without Upstash-NonRetryable-Error is retried
means: A 489 without the Upstash-NonRetryable-Error header is a failed delivery like any other non-2XX answer, retried on the backoff.

title: Timeout rule: a compound duration, 1d1h30m, on the Pay as you go plan
means: Upstash-Timeout's own example 1d1h30m (spec:post_v2_publish_destination's examples: 5s, 2m, 1h, 1d1h30m) is accepted, and since it "can be used to shorten the default allowed timeout value on your plan", one longer than the plan's Max HTTP Response Duration (Pay as you go: 2 hours, https://upstash.com/pricing/qstash) waits the plan's two hours: an answer that takes three is given up on at two, still unanswered at one hour fifty-nine. With no retries left the message is in the DLQ, and its failure callback carries its sourceMessageId and dlqId.

title: Flow control rule: a call holds its parallelism slot until its response is received
means: "Active means that the call is made to your endpoint and the response is not received yet": with parallelism 1, the second message waits until the first call's answer arrives, ten seconds later when the endpoint takes ten seconds to answer, and is then delivered.
